question:
Below are two chemical equations:

Zn (s) + CuSO₄ (aq) → ZnSO₄ (aq) + Cu (s)

Pb (s) + CuCl₂ (aq) → PbCl₂ (aq) + Cu (s)

Why does copper get separated from its compound form in both the cases?

options.text: Zinc and Lead are unstable in element form.
Copper compounds break down under high pressure.
Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.
Copper is more reactive than Zinc and Lead.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc and Lead are more reactive than Copper.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Zinc and Lead are higher in the reactivity series than Copper, making them more reactive elements.
 
• In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal will displace a less reactive metal from its compound.
 
• When Zinc reacts with Copper sulfate (CuSO₄), Zinc displaces Copper because Zinc is more reactive.
 
• Similarly, Lead displaces Copper from Copper chloride (CuCl₂) due to its higher reactivity compared to Copper.
 
• This reactivity series is a fundamental concept in chemistry for predicting the outcomes of displacement reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• It helps in predicting the products of displacement reactions and the reactivity of metals with acids and water.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reactions**
 
 
• These are reactions where a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• They are commonly observed in aqueous solutions of metal salts.
 
 
 
• **Electrochemical Series**
 
 
• It is a series of elements arranged by their standard electrode potentials.
 
• It is useful in predicting the direction of redox reactions.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Zinc and Lead**
 
 
• Zinc is used for galvanizing iron, making alloys, and in batteries.
 
• Lead is used in batteries, radiation shielding, and in some types of glass.
